name: countdown
title: Launch countdown
summary: "Launch in HH:MM:SS" counting down to a fixed UTC instant, computed from the day of the year, the local time and offsetToUtc().
prompt: Make a launch countdown timer showing hours, minutes and seconds left until a fixed date and time in UTC.
teaches: Convert local time to UTC with offsetToUtc(): utc = local - offsetToUtc(), so remaining = target - local + offsetToUtc()
Keep float precision by subtracting day and second-of-day parts separately: (targetDay - dayOfYear()) * 86400 + (targetSec - secondOfDay)
Name the remaining seconds once in resources.variables and split it into hours, minutes and seconds with floor and %

snippets.note: seconds to 2026-10-29 12:24:12 UTC (day 302, second 44652), clamped at 0

check.describe: At 2026-10-29 10:10:05 UTC (epoch ms 1793268605000) it reads 02:14:07 in any time zone; at the launch instant and after, 00:00:00. Resized, the column stays centred both ways and keeps its three lines.

pitfalls: Pin the clock as epoch milliseconds: a "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" clock is local time, so the instant, and a countdown to a UTC moment, shift with the renderer's time zone
epochSecond() converts with json2rc but the Java parser does not know it; build absolute time from dayOfYear(), timeInMin(), timeInSec() and offsetToUtc() instead
A float has 24 bits of mantissa: seconds-since-Jan-1 (~3e7) lose whole seconds, so subtract the target's day and second-of-day separately; the formula only works within one calendar year
Hours are floor(@remaining / 3600) with no % 24: past 99 hours whole 2 drops the leading digit, so add a days field (or whole 3) for a longer countdown
